Entries.Text: First Person
First Person

Walk around the loaded maps at head height, colliding with their collision and the collision of their assets. Pick where the player starts by clicking in the viewport. The collision is read from the game files, so it works whether or not collision is displayed.
First person isn't supported for this game yet.
Collision loading is turned off in the Map Editor's settings, so there is no collision to walk on. Turn it on and load a map again.
Load a map to walk around it.
Spawn
Where the player starts. The sphere marks the feet; the capsule above it is the space the player takes up.
No spawn set.
Checking the spawn once the collision is built.
The spawn is on walkable ground, with room for the player.
The spawn is on a surface too steep to stand on. Pick a flatter spot, or raise the walkable slope under Player.
The player doesn't fit at the spawn: the capsule runs into a wall or ceiling. Pick a more open spot.
There is no collision below the spawn.
The position of the player's feet. A typed position is checked where it is, without dropping it onto the ground.
Pick Spawn
Click in the viewport to place the spawn on the collision under the cursor. A preview follows the cursor, green where the player can stand and red where they can't.
Cancel Picking
Stop picking, keeping the current spawn.
Spawn Below Camera
Place the spawn on the collision straight below the viewport camera.
Spawn Below Selection
Place the spawn on the collision below the selection, for example a player start point.
Clear Spawn
Remove the spawn.
Click in the viewport to place the spawn.
Building the collision. You can click to place the spawn once it is done.
The collision is still being built. Click again once it is done.
There is no collision under the cursor. Click on ground the player can stand on.
There is no collision below that point.
Walk
Walk the map from the spawn, in the viewport you last used. The camera turns with the mouse and stays at the player's eyes. Leaving puts the camera back where it was.
Enter First Person
Start walking from the spawn. The mouse is taken by the viewport until you press the release key.
Exit First Person
Stop walking and put the camera back where it was.
Walking. Press {0} to release the mouse.
Paused: the player stands still. Click in the viewport to carry on, or press {0} again to leave.
The player fell out of the loaded collision and was put back at the spawn.
The collision is still being built.
Pick a spawn first.
The player can't stand at the spawn. Pick another spot.
There is no collision to walk on. Build it first.
Click in a viewport first, so the tool knows which one to walk in.
Controls
The keys while walking. They are set in the keybinds settings. While the mouse is captured, the editor's other shortcuts are off.
Run: hold {0}
Jump: {0}
Look: move the mouse
Noclip (fly through walls, where you look; Jump rises): {0}
Teleport to the crosshair: {0}
Noclip ({0} to land)
The collision was rebuilt, as a map was loaded or unloaded, collision was edited, or an option changed. You're walking on the new collision.
Noclip: flying through everything. Press the noclip key again to land where you are.
Can't land here: the player is inside something. Fly into the open, then try again.
Nothing under the crosshair to teleport to.
No room to stand where the crosshair points.
Release the mouse and pause: {0}; again to leave
First person: {0} to release the mouse
First person paused: click to carry on, {0} to leave
Display
What the viewport shows while walking, and where the camera is left afterwards.
Hide Editor Helpers
While walking, hide what the game doesn't draw: collision, navmeshes, regions, lights, dummies and other editor markers. They come back when you leave.
Crosshair
Show a small cross at the centre of the viewport while walking.
Show Surface Underfoot
While walking, show the collision material under the player's feet: its HitMtrlParam row (the surface's sounds and effects) and its property (Safe, Slide), as the Collision Generator names them.
Surface: {0}
in the air
flying
no material (a primitive shape, or an older game's mesh)
Leave Camera Where You Walked
On leaving, keep the camera at the player's eyes instead of putting it back where it was before walking.
Collision

The collision the player walks on, built from the loaded maps: collision parts with the player's hit filter (HitFilterID 8; Map in DS2) and the collision of assets. It is built when you pick a spawn, and again when a map is loaded or unloaded, collision is edited, or the options below change.
Building: {0} / {1}
The collision couldn't be built. See the log for the error.
Not built yet. It is built when you pick a spawn.
{0} maps: {1} collision parts, {2} triangles.
{0} collision parts left out: they aren't the player's (HitFilterID other than {1}).
{0} parts use the other layer, as they have none of this one; {1} have no collision.
Assets: {0} placements of {1} models, {2} triangles.
{0} MB, built in {1} s.
{0} files couldn't be read. See the log.
Out of date: rebuilt when you next pick a spawn, or with Build.
Build
Build the collision of the loaded maps again now.
Collision Layer
Which of the maps' collision the player collides with.

Low collision is the rougher of the two and much lighter to build. High is detailed, but in a legacy dungeon it can take ten times the triangles and several hundred MB. A part without the chosen layer uses the other.
Fall Protection
Also collide with the fall protection walls along ledges.
Asset Collision

Also collide with the collision of assets and objects. Many maps are built mostly from assets, so turning this off can leave little to stand on. Breakable objects with no collision of their own are walked through.
Dummy Assets
Also collide with dummy assets, which are stand-ins for cutscenes and aren't collided with in the game.
Player
The size of the player and the slopes they can stand on.
Eye Height: %.2f m
How far above the feet the camera is.
Height: %.2f m
The height of the player's capsule. It is kept above the eye height.
Radius: %.2f m
The radius of the player's capsule: how close they can come to walls.
Walkable Slope: %.0f deg
The steepest ground the player can stand on, in degrees from flat.
Movement
How fast the player walks and runs, how high they jump, and the steps they climb without jumping.
Walk Speed: %.1f m/s
How fast the player walks.
Run Speed: %.1f m/s
How fast the player moves while running. It is never slower than walking.
Jump Height: %.2f m
How high the player's feet rise at the top of a jump.
Gravity: %.1f m/s/s
How quickly the player falls. Higher than real gravity (9.8) makes jumps feel quicker, as in games.
Step Height: %.2f m
The highest step or kerb the player walks up without jumping.
Slide Surfaces Can't Be Stood On

Ground whose collision material has the Slide property (Slide1, Slide2) is treated as too steep to stand on, so the player slides off it. How the game treats Slide surfaces isn't confirmed; turn this off to stand on them.
Reset Player
Set the player's size, walkable slope and movement back to their defaults.
